steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Analytical writing about film moves beyond personal opinion to sustained, evidence-based argument about how meaning is constructed. | Key Fact: Every claim in a film essay must be supported by specific evidence from the film: name the technique, describe its use and explain its effect. | Key Fact: Evaluative writing requires you to make a judgement and justify it, weighing evidence and considering alternative interpretations before reaching a conclusion. | Key Fact: Structure is essential: an introduction establishing your argument, focused body paragraphs each making one point, and a conclusion that synthesises your reasoning.
